exposure: Type of surgery (open, laparoscopic, laparoscopic converted to open)
cohort: 427 patients who underwent upper gastrointestinal surgery at Royal North Shore Hospital (Sydney, Australia) between November 2015 and October 2020
finding: While thoracic epidural analgesia was superior to intrathecal morphine and non-neuraxial analgesia for reducing postoperative morphine requirements and improving pain control, its benefits did not last beyond postoperative day 2, and it was associated with higher rates of hypotension and technique failure.
